links.outcome: Ability of ED clinicians to find and launch the CDS tool within the workflow
links.effect: Main interface had high perceived usability, but participants struggled to find the launch button; poor launch button visibility impaired uptake (3% utilization in first 3 months).
links.quote: Although the main user interface had high perceived usability, participants struggled to find the launch button.

links.outcome: Availability of risk model and evidence information to clinicians at point of use
links.effect: When the recommendation mismatched clinical gestalt, participants needed more information about the risk model and evidence, which was not readily available; this lowered perceived utility.
links.quote: When there was mismatch, perceived utility was lower, and participants needed more information about the risk model and supporting evidence, which were not readily available.

links.outcome: Tool uptake and usability barriers after human-centered design and implementation strategies
links.effect: Despite human-centered design and implementation science strategies, initial utilization in the first 3 months was just 3%; usability and contextual barriers identified.
links.quote: Despite applying human-centered design and implementation science strategies, initial utilization in the first 3 months of the STRATIFY-CDS tool was just 3%.

unlisted_practices: Simulation-based training as an implementation strategy to build initial confidence in CDS
Establishing social norms among clinicians for CDS use

screen.reason: Evaluates barriers to uptake and usability of an implemented clinical decision support tool calculating an acute heart failure risk prediction model in the emergency department using post-deployment clinician interviews and simulations.
